elasticstack_fleet_agent_download_source.reason: Real user-configurable feature (authenticating to a private download host with api_key, basic auth, or custom headers); the resource has no auth support today and no opaque attribute covers it, so this should be exposed.

Real user-configurable feature letting auth/ssl material for a download source be stored as a Fleet secret instead of plaintext; no opaque attribute or existing field covers this, so it should be exposed.

Real user-configurable feature (custom certificate/CA/key for a download host using self-signed or private certs); the resource has no SSL support today and no opaque attribute covers it, so this should be exposed.

elasticstack_fleet_agent_policy#/compone.reason: The advanced_settings block already mirrors most of this API sub-object (logging, download, go_max_procs, monitoring_runtime_experimental); these remaining agent feature toggles are a natural, low-risk extension of an attribute the resource already partially exposes, not computed or imperative fields.

elasticstack_fleet_custom_integration#/p.reason: List-catalog filter for browsing by category; irrelevant once a package is identified by exact name+version.
List-catalog filter for UI browsing by install status; not meaningful when the resource already targets a specific name+version.
Server-computed display count of package policies; purely informational and unrelated to resource configuration.
Only toggles inclusion of optional descriptive/display metadata (readme, screenshots, assets) in the read response; none of that data is surfaced by this resource.

Custom integrations are locally uploaded, EPR-unverified packages; the read step calls GetPackage without ignoreUnverified, so Kibana can reject reads for genuinely unsigned custom packages. Worth exposing so users can opt into tolerating unverified signatures on read.

elasticstack_fleet_elastic_defend_integr.reason: Grants the agent policy extra data-stream write permissions beyond the endpoint package's own streams; a real, user-controllable Fleet feature not represented in the resource schema.

Top-level agent condition expression lets a policy be conditionally applied (e.g. by agent OS/version); this is a genuine, user-controllable Fleet feature with no current representation in the resource schema.

Defend always builds one hardcoded endpoint input with an always-empty streams list, configuring everything through the opaque config/policy/advanced_settings mechanism instead of vars; the flagged input- and stream-level fields assume a multi-input/stream shape that does not apply here.

experimental_data_stream_features, fips_compatible, and requires_root describe intrinsic properties of the installed package build (determined by name/version), not independent choices a policy author makes, and the package has no data streams of its own.
Defend does not use the generic package vars/var-group mechanism; its full configuration surface is already exposed via the policy, advanced_settings, and preset attributes.
Query parameter controlling the wire format (legacy vs simplified) of the request/response body; internal API plumbing, not a Terraform-manageable attribute of the policy.

elasticstack_fleet_integration#/componen.reason: Sibling install-behavior toggle (force, prerelease, ignore_constraints) already exposed for this resource's required version attribute; allow_outdated_version is the same class of user-controllable flag and is missing from InstallPackageOptions.

elasticstack_fleet_integration_policy#/c.reason: experimental_data_stream_features is a genuine user-configurable, infrastructure-affecting setting not covered by vars_json or any existing attribute; filed alongside the bundled fips_compatible/requires_root descriptors.

elasticstack_fleet_managed_integration#/.reason: Already fully implemented: schema.go has a cloud_connector block, models_convert.go builds it via a raw map into body.CloudConnector, and cloud_connector_read.go merges enabled/cloud_connector_id from the API; the AST scanner missed it because the fields are assigned dynamically rather than via named struct fields.

experimental_data_stream_features is a genuine user-configurable override (synthetic_source/tsdb/doc_value_only per data stream), not yet exposed anywhere in the package block (schema.go only has name/version/title); worth adding alongside fips_compatible and requires_root.

v7format is a query parameter on the unrelated internal GET /api/status preflight call (topology.go) used only to detect serverless/cloud build flavor; it controls response envelope format, not any resource configuration, so it has no place in a Terraform schema.
Same /api/status preflight call as v7format; purely a response-format version flag for an internal status check, not a configurable resource field.

elasticstack_fleet_output#/components/sc.reason: allow_edit lists which fields a kibana.yml-preconfigured output may still be edited through, which only has meaning for preconfigured outputs; it is server-managed state irrelevant to outputs created and fully owned through the API/Terraform.
is_internal flags outputs Fleet itself creates and manages internally; it is server-computed state, not something a user sets when creating an output.
is_preconfigured indicates the output originated from kibana.yml static config rather than the API; it is computed/reported state that doesn't apply to API/Terraform-managed outputs.

This is a real per-output toggle with functional effect on the compiled agent policy (controls auth behavior in the OTel exporter pipeline), not server-managed state or UI bookkeeping, and is entirely absent from schema.go/models.go for every output type.

The secrets container stores sensitive fields (e.g. ssl.key) via Fleet secret storage instead of plaintext; models_ssl.go only ever sets the plaintext ssl.key and there is no secret-reference path for any output type, unlike the precedent already set for the kafka password field.

elasticstack_fleet_proxy#/paths/~1api~1f.reason: Server-managed flag indicating a kibana.yml-defined proxy; the resource already exposes it as a computed, read-only attribute, consistent with it never appearing in request bodies.

elasticstack_fleet_server_host#/paths/~1.reason: allow_edit is a user-settable allowlist (POST and PUT bodies) controlling which fields remain editable on this host, independent of server-managed preconfiguration flags; not covered by any existing attribute.
is_internal marks server hosts created for internal Kibana/Fleet bookkeeping purposes rather than user-managed infrastructure; not a meaningful knob for Terraform-authored hosts.
secrets lets users reference existing Kibana secrets for SSL key material instead of plaintext; the resource currently has no SSL/TLS support at all, a real functionality gap.
ssl carries certificate/key/client_auth configuration for the Fleet Server host connection; the resource exposes no TLS attributes today, a significant gap for production use.

elasticstack_kibana_action_connector#/co.reason: Genuine user-configurable capability (turning inbound-event receiving on/off for bidirectional connectors) that sits on a sibling top-level request field, not inside the resource's generic config JSON object, so the existing opaque config attribute cannot reach it; no code comment disclaims it, so it should be exposed.

elasticstack_kibana_agentbuilder_agent#/.reason: access_control is entirely unexposed: grep for access_control/AccessControl across internal/kibana/agentbuilderagent (schema.go, models.go, create.go, update.go) finds no references. It is a user-controllable permissions setting on the agent, not server-managed state, so it belongs in Terraform.

Configuration sub-fields (ai_indices, connector_ids, plugin_ids, workflow_ids, subagent_ids, enable_elastic_capabilities, approvals.auto_approved_apis) control which indices, connectors, plugins, workflows, and subagents the agent can use; none are exposed in the Terraform schema (confirmed in internal/kibana/agentbuilderagent/models.go, where the anonymous Configuration struct declares these fields but only Instructions, Tools, and SkillIds are ever populated) or covered by any opaque attribute, so this is a real, user-controllable gap.

elasticstack_kibana_agentbuilder_skill#/.reason: Real, user-meaningful delete-time option (cascade-remove the skill from referencing agents instead of failing with 409); the implementation's own code comment flags this as a deliberate v1 omission still pending exposure, so it is a legitimate follow-up to file.

elasticstack_kibana_agentbuilder_tool#/p.reason: confirmation (askUser: always/never/once) is a real, user-controllable tool-call safety policy on create and update; it is entirely unmodeled in schema.go/models.go with no comment explaining the omission and no opaque attribute covers it, so it should be exposed.
